requirements.requirement: Export node1:/srv/nfs/shared and mount it at /mnt/shared on node2.
requirements.summary: node1 actively exports the requested path to node2, and node2 has an active NFS mount at /mnt/shared. The mount and export remained functional after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Use the dataops identity with UID and GID 4500 on both systems.
requirements.summary: Both nodes directly report dataops as UID 4500 and primary GID 4500, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set the shared directory to dataops:dataops with mode 2770 and preserve consistent ownership and permissions for files created from either system.
requirements.summary: The shared directory is UID/GID 4500:4500 with mode 2770. Files created as dataops from node1 and node2 were visible on both systems with UID/GID 4500:4500 and mode 660; additional post-restart writes behaved consistently.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic. Distribution-provided NFS packages for that release were installed and operated successfully.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and cross-node behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for both managed nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered identity, service, mount/export, data, and write behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with the executor observations.
limitations: Systemd failed-service checks were unsupported on this legacy release, and the lifecycle socket inventory did not expose service details. Direct RPC, export, mount, file-access, and package-health observations nevertheless provide coherent service-health evidence.

The legacy package manager reported that downloaded packages could not be authenticated during installation. The packages came from the configured Ubuntu old-releases repository and were shown operational, but the captured evidence does not independently verify package signatures.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package-index refreshes and NFS package installations established required prerequisites; account, directory, export, and mount changes directly implemented the task; test-file writes provided bounded behavioral and restart evidence. The initially failing node2 verification command still created the intended test file, which subsequent commands verified, so it contributed to the outcome rather than being an unrelated experiment. Restart-request logs left no observed /tmp residue after reboot, package-manager health remained clean, and no abandoned or conflicting state was captured.
